about: Wing designs for flyers whose static draws no wing (flyer_gate.NO_WINGS_DRAWN, gate G3). A design is what a body master and its wing layers are prompted from (study design/RimMandrake/flyer_stable_body_study.md 3.3 and 3.4); `flyer_gate.py wingprompt DEF FACING master|up|level|down` renders the prompt. The redraw itself is owed by the flyer's tier item. Item THOZZIK_REDRAW_WINGS_FLIES_WITHOUT_THEM.

RM_Thozzik.label: thozzik
RM_Thozzik.look: an armoured hive insect of the Rot: glossy oxblood-red segmented carapace, six jointed legs, a pair of serrated pincer forelimbs, its back crowded with cream fungal toxin sacs and small orange mushroom caps
RM_Thozzik.why_wings: MaxFlightTime 30: short hive-to-prey hops. The family's wings are the queen's (RM_ThozzikQueen draws them in every facing), smaller on the worker so they never hide the fungal back the description is about
RM_Thozzik.wings: four short membranous wings in two pairs, forewing longer than hindwing, translucent dusky amber with dark red veins and a ragged, spore-pitted trailing edge, matching the Thozzik queen's wings
RM_Thozzik.roots: both pairs rise from the hard shoulder plate just behind the head, in front of the fungal mass, so every root is visible and nothing grows over it
RM_Thozzik.folded: folded flat and narrow along each flank, below the line of the fungal sacs and above the legs, tips reaching the rear of the abdomen; the fungal back, the pincers and all six legs stay fully visible

facings.east: side view; the near forewing lies along the flank, the hindwing a sliver beneath it
facings.south: front view; the folded wings show only as two thin amber edges at the shoulders beside the head
facings.north: back view; the folded wings show as two thin amber strips along each side of the fungal back

poses.up: both pairs raised in a V above the fungal back, tips above the highest mushroom cap
poses.level: both pairs spread straight out sideways at shoulder height, forewing ahead of hindwing
poses.down: both pairs swept down below the belly line, tips beside the middle legs

RM_Thozzik.blur: a translucent amber blur disc variant of the level pose (insect plan, study 3.3)

RSW_Strill.label: strill
RSW_Strill.look: a one-metre six-legged predator from Mandalore: thick gold to gray-tan fur, loose folds of leathery skin draped along flanks, back and haunches, four ears, gold eyes, an enormous fanged maw, a thin whip-like tail
RSW_Strill.why_wings: No wings in canon. Legends: skin folds 'form wing membranes between their six strong legs' to glide and 'even fly short distances by flapping their legs in unison'. Owner 2026-10-17 (canon entry Must show): 'Note the whip-like tail. Enormously toothy maw. Four ears. Six legs.  Gliding flyers.'
RSW_Strill.wings: glide membranes of loose leathery skin, a tan-brown patagium spanning foreleg to middle leg to hind leg on each side and running back to the base of the whip tail; fur-edged, thin enough to show the leg bones as ribs
RSW_Strill.roots: each membrane is the flank skin itself, joined along the whole side of the body from shoulder to hip; the six leg joints are its anchor points and stay visible
RSW_Strill.folded: on the ground the membranes hang slack as the loose pleated skin folds along each flank between the six legs; all six legs stand clear and are each visible as a separate leg

facings.east: side view; six legs, three per side visible (near three in front, far three partly behind), slack skin pleats sagging between them
facings.south: front view; the head with four ears and the fanged maw, the two front legs and the middle legs splayed a little, skin folds visible at the flanks
facings.north: back view; the furred back, the whip tail, the hind legs, slack skin folds at both flanks; never a sliver, the body at least a third as wide as the side view is long

poses.up: all six legs raised together above the back line, membranes stretched upward in a shallow V
poses.level: all six legs splayed straight out sideways, membranes taut and flat like a flying squirrel's
poses.down: all six legs swept down together below the belly, membranes cupped beneath the body

RSW_Strill.layer_note: The membrane moves with the legs, so in the glider plan a wing layer is the six legs with their membranes; the body plate pinned across frames is torso, head and tail. The flight body is a separate master from the ground static (legs splayed), the same individual and markings.
